is to build stronger communities by providing opportunities for development and active, healthy
living committed to all. Its ten YMCA centers, its international language school, its ski school, its

each year by more than 130,000 people. The first YMCA in America Nord was founded in Montreal
in November 1851. The YMCAs of Quebec are part of a network Canadian which has 50 YMCA
associations. For more information, visit our site Internet www.ymcaquebec.org, our Facebook
pages facebook.com/ymcaquebec or Twitter twitter.com/YMCAQuebec.

Organization 2: Côte-des-Neiges community leisure center - Celo URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centrecommunautairedeloisirdelacotedesneiges/
Website: http://www.cclcdn.qc.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5347,
chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, Montreal QC H3T 1Y4 514 733-1478 514 733-7481 Opening hours
SCHEDULE The center is open to all: Monday to Sunday from 9 a.m. to the end of activities
Mission Offer to residents of the Côte-des-Neiges a unifying, harmonious and participatory living
environment, aiming for fulfillment personal and collective development, through leisure, popular
education and action community. Description Origin of our organization In the midst of the Olympic
period, citizens from the neighborhood founded the Center. The founding members wanted to react
to the shortage of services recreational activities in the neighborhood and meet the leisure needs of
the population. The City of Montreal is closely associated with the founding of the Center. She rents
from the C.E.C.M. 5347 which was unoccupied and lends the building to the Corporation du Center
Récréatif Notre-Dame-des-Neiges (the name of the Center for incorporation). Our main
achievements Over the years, the Center has asserted forces leisure as a tool for social integration,
as an agent for preventing social dropout and maintaining physical and mental health. Since its
founding, it has joined a number considerable number of people. Now, in the Center’s animation
team, we find young people who have attended our activities since they were 4-5 years old. These
young people were able to develop their knowledge, their “leadership” and have integrated into
community life.

Organization 5: 12th Notre-Dame-de-Grâce scout group URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/12egroupescoutnotredamedegrace/ Website: None
Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5333, Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Montreal
QC H4A 1L2 514-486-6433 Opening hours SCHEDULE Castors (7-8 years): Monday from 6:00
p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Cub Scout girls (9-11 years old): Wednesday from 6:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Cub
Scout boys (9-11 years old): Thursday from 6:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Girls Scouts (11-14 years old):
Monday from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Boys Scouts (11-14 years): Tuesday from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00
p.m. Pioneers (14-17 years): Thursday from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Networks social Contacts (1)
SCOUT REGISTRATION Communicate with this contact Mission Scouting Montrealer's mission is
the dynamic education of boys and girls, by allowing them to create and experience high-challenge
projects promoting the development of leadership and involvement in the community. We help
young people to become committed people, responsible, autonomous and supportive thanks to a
game-based methodology. For registration : inscription@scoutndg.org Description The 12th group
brings together the following 7 units: * Beavers Mixed 7 and 8 years old Among the beavers, in the
very heart of nature, young people will learn resourcefulness and team spirit. * Cub Scouts Girls 9
to 11 years old * Cub Scouts Boys 9 to 11 years old Akéla, this wise wolf will take young people on
all kinds of adventures in the heart of the jungle. From Great challenges, games and activities await
young people. * Girl Scouts 11 to 14 years old * Scouts Boys 11 to 14 years old Team spirit,
resourcefulness and personal challenges, these are the scout issues. Activities of the year: camp in
all seasons and outdoor techniques. * Pioneers Mixed 14 to 17 years old * Rover Scouts Mixed 17
to 25 years old Autonomy is the watchword of pioneers. They are the ones who choose and
prepare each of their activities. For registrations: registration@scoutndg.org

Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4700, Belmore, Montreal QC H4V 1V9
Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday evening: Cub Scouts (boys 9-11 years old) Tuesday evening:
Cub Scouts (girls 9-11 years old) Wednesday evening: Castors (mixed 7-8 years old) AND Kampis
(mixed 15-17 years old) Thursday evening: Scouts (mixed 12-14 year olds) Social networks Mission
Montreal scouting’s mission is the dynamic education of young people, allowing them to create and
experience high-challenge projects promoting leadership development and community involvement.
We help the young people to become committed, responsible, autonomous and supportive people
thanks to methodology based on play, team and nature. Description The 132nd group
Sainte-Catherine-de-Sienne is made up of a team of around twenty volunteer facilitators who
supervises around sixty young people. Our group is a member of the World Organization of
Scouting through the Association des Scouts du Canada. Scouting is an activity extracurricular in
which one undertakes, among other things, to participate in an activity session by week (in the
evening) and various other one-off activities, including overnight camps outside the city.

Organization 7: 229th Notre-Dame-des-Neiges scout group URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/229egroupescoutnotredamedesneiges/ Website:
http://www.scouts229.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5366 Chemin
De La Côte-des-Neiges, Montreal QC H3T 1Y4 514-733-4174 Opening hours SCHEDULE Castors
Friday 6:30 p.m. Hirondelles Thursday, from 6:30 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. Cub Scouts Monday, from 6
p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Cubs Wednesday 18 30 p.m. Scouts and pioneers Tuesday, 7 p.m. to 9 p.m.
Intrepids and pioneers Sunday, 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. h Road workers Sunday 5 p.m. Contacts (1)
FRANÇOIS CARON-MELANÇON Group leader 514 961-9232 Communicate with this contact
Mission The Scout Movement is an educational movement based on volunteerism. The aim of
scouting is to contribute to the development of young people by helping to fully realize their
possibilities as people, according to the principles defined by the founder Lord Robert
Baden-Powell. It is a non-political movement, open to all, without distinction of origin or belief.
Description Activities Weekly meetings in evening from September to June Winter camp: one
weekend for each unit Summer camp: one weekend for each unit Various outings and activities
throughout the year Costs Annual contribution depending on the units. Scouting is an educational
movement open to all. He encourages young people to take charge of their own progress. The
objective is to allow young people to develop all facets of their personality (physical, social,
emotional, intellectual and spiritual) through the game, the team, nature, commitment, and
celebration. This way so that he later becomes an autonomous adult, capable of engaging in
society with the aim of to improve it. Young people are supervised by responsible adults trained to
guide them, support and encourage them in all their endeavors. In each unit the number of young
people is limited in order to respect a facilitator/young person ration of 1/8. Even if the scout year
goes from September to September, registrations are done at any time and, depending on the
availability of places in the unit, a young person can start at any time of the year. Every young
person has the right to a trial period of three meetings.

Organization 9: Westhaven-Elmhurst Community Association URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/association-communautaire-westhaven-elmhurst/
Website: None Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 7405 avenue Harley,
Montréal QC H4B 1L5 514 872-6134 Opening hours SCHEDULE variable Mission Offer
recreational activities for all ages, to support teenagers and pre-teens, and to create a space
inclusive and dynamic community in Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Montreal. Together,
we strengthen family and intergenerational ties for a more united future. Description The
Westhaven-Elmhurst Community Association is a dynamic organization located in
Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Montreal. Committed to offering a range of activities
recreational, this association is aimed at a wide clientele, including young people, families, adults
and elderly people. At the Westhaven-Elmhurst Community Association, we believe firmly in the
importance of social cohesion and community well-being. This is why we offer several services
adapted to different age groups, aiming to promote integration and personal development. Our
main recreational activities include: programs intended for adults and children, promoting physical
activity and social connections. A service dedicated to adolescents and pre-adolescents, offering
learning and leisure. A summer camp for young people, designed to encourage creativity and
teamwork in a fun and safe environment. We strive to create an inclusive environment where each
individual can flourish, learn and have fun. Thanks to our diversified activities, we aim to strengthen
ties between community members, while meeting the needs specific to each. We invite you to join
us to discover all the opportunities that the Westhaven-Elmhurst Community Association has to
offer. Together, let's build a stronger and more united community!

Organization 10: Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Minor Hockey Association URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/associationdehockeymineurdenotredamed egrace/
Website: http://www.ndghockey.com/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details
4985, Avenue West Hill, Montréal QC H4V 2W6 514-487-6799 514-487-9698 Mission The mission
of the Minor Hockey Association of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is to promote community development
through hockey minor. Serving the Côte-des-Neiges and Nôtre-Dame-de-Grâce neighborhoods in
Montreal, our objective is to promote inclusion, sport and the well-being of young people.
Description Association of minor hockey of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (NDG) is a community
organization based in Montreal, Canada, which is dedicated to the development of minor hockey in
the neighborhoods of Côte-des-Neiges and Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. The association welcomes
young players from different levels and organizes various events throughout the year to promote
sport, camaraderie and fair play. Services offered: Registrations for the 2024-2025 season
Participation minor hockey tournaments Player development programs Training opportunities
volunteering for the community The association is led by a dedicated president who strives to
ensure that each hockey season is memorable for players, coaches and families. Upcoming events:
December 2 – December 15, 2024: NDG hockey tournament September 2025: Start of the
2025-2026 season Stay informed of the latest news and events by following the association on
social media: Facebook: NDG Minor Hockey Twitter: @hockeyndg Instagram: NDG Minor Hockey
For any questions or information additional information, please contact the association: Contact
details: Address: 4985, West Hill Avenue, Montreal, Quebec H4V 2W6 Telephone: (514) 487-6799
Email: info@ndghockey.com

Organization 12: Region 2 Netball Association URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/associationdenetballregion2/ Website: None
Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 514 486-2769 The email address of this
organization is unknown, please contact them by phone. This organization belongs? Claim
management of this file! Mission Encourage the practice of netball within of the Nan community by
offering quality programs for all levels. We aim to promote an active and healthy lifestyle, to
promote inclusion and development personal through sport. Join us for an enriching and stimulating
experience with the Region 2 Netball Association. Description The Region 2 Netball Association is
a community organization based in nan, dedicated to promoting netball in the region. Our mission is
to promote the practice of this sport within the local community, by offering training, competition and
gathering opportunities for netball enthusiasts. We operate mainly in the fields of sport and leisure,
offering varied activities for the members of our association. Whether you are a beginner player or
experienced, you will find with us a friendly and dynamic environment to practice netball and
develop your skills. Our services include: Netball lessons for all levels Friendly matches and
regional competitions Sporting and social events Join the Region 2 Netball Association to live an
enriching and stimulating experience in the heart of the community. Together, let's cultivate our
passion for this sport and create lasting links through netball to nan.

Organization 13: Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Ringette Association URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/associationderinguettedenotredamedegrace/
Website: http://www.ndgringuette.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details
514 481-1295 Mission Offering to young people of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce the opportunity to get
involved in a dynamic and inclusive team sport what is ringette. By promoting the personal
development, health and well-being of our members, we help strengthen the social fabric of our
community. Join us for experience unforgettable moments and create lasting bonds! Description
The Ringette Association de Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is a community organization committed to
promoting sport and leisure in the city of nan. Our mission is to promote personal development and
physical fitness of young people through the practice of ringette, a dynamic and stimulating team
sport. As a ringette club, we offer quality supervised training programs by passionate and
experienced coaches. We also organize competitions and sporting events to allow our members to
surpass themselves and experience moments unforgettable on the ice. We are proud to be part of
the community of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and contribute to the well-being of its inhabitants. In
addition to promoting the sporting practice, we encourage team spirit, solidarity and respect for the
values of the sport among our members. The areas of intervention of our association include:
Organization ringette competitions Youth training programs Ringette promotion in the community
We are convinced that ringette is a sport accessible to all and beneficial for health and well-being.
Join the Ringette Association Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and discover the pleasure of playing as a team
while developing your sports skills.

Organization 14: Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Soccer Association URL:

Organization 15: Saint-Raymond Community Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-communautaire-de-saint-raymond/ Website:
https://cjndg.org/fr/accueil Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5600 chemin
Upper-Lachine, Montréal QC H4A 2A7 514 872-1765 Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday
1:00 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mission Our mission at the NDG Youth
Committee is to build a strong and healthy community by improving the quality of life of its
residents. We offer diverse and stimulating programs, promoting inclusion and well-being for all.
Committed to meet the changing needs of the community, we work collaboratively with our partners
to offer essential activities and promote a balanced lifestyle. Description Saint Raymond
Community Center Saint Raymond Community Center, a organization committed to improving the
quality of life of the neighborhood community Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. Our mission is to provide a
welcoming and inclusive space for residents of all ages. About us The Saint Raymond Community
Center is part of of the Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Youth Committee (CJNDG), which works in
collaboration with the City of Montreal to offer stimulating and varied programs. We emphasize
diversity culture of our neighborhood and aim to create a strong and healthy community. Our
services Recreational and sporting activities: We offer activities for all ages, from children to
seniors, in order to promote a healthy and active lifestyle. Community Support: We are there to
support residents in different aspects of their lives, whether through educational programs, family
support or other services. Multicultural programs: We celebrate the diversity of our neighborhood by
offering programs that reflect the different cultures present in our community. Board of Directors
Our Board of Directors is made up of dedicated members who work for the well-being of the
community. Among them, we find community leaders, committed volunteers and experts in various
domains. Brian O’Connell: Community leader with over 25 years of experience. He has contributed
to many local programs. Simeon Pompey: Animation director involved in the community for over 40
years. Eddy Taylor: Consultant and active volunteer in the hockey association for over 20 years.
Michelle Riffin: Board Member providing its expertise in human resources. Stephen De Four-Wyre:
Lawyer specializing in immigration, also university lecturer. Michael Held: Retired entrepreneur
involved in the community for 47 years. We are proud of our diverse team who work together to
offer quality services to the community of Saint Raymond and its surrounding areas. Contact For
more information about our services and programs, do not hesitate to contact us contact:
Telephone: 514.123.4567 Email: info@saintraymondcentre.org

Organization 16: Iraqi Community Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-communautaire-irakien/ Website:
https://iraqicommunitycenter.com/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 6767
Chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, Bureau 604-1, Montréal QC H3S 2T6 514 823-4727 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Monday: 10:00 – 1:00 p.m. Tuesday: Closed Wednesday: Closed Thursday: 05:30 –
20:00 Friday: Closed Saturday: Closed Sunday: Closed Mission Accompany and support the Iraqi
community of Montreal in facilitating access to housing, employment and organizing community
activities. We we also represent the interests of our community to local authorities and national.
Description The Iraqi Community Center is an organization dedicated to assistance from the Iraqi
community residing in Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Montreal. This organization plays
an essential role by offering various services and organizing activities that strengthen ties within the
community. Among the main missions of Center, we find: Housing search assistance to help
families find a place to settle comfortably. Job search assistance to support members of the
community in their professional integration. Organization of community activities for promote
exchanges and sharing of culture between members. Representation to local and national bodies,
ensuring that community concerns are heard. Conferences on important issues affecting the
community, providing information and raise awareness among members on key topics. Clientele
served by the Center Iraqi Community consists mainly of people who are part of the community
Iraqi. This audience is at the heart of all initiatives, because the Center aims to meet the needs
specific and the challenges encountered by these individuals. By providing a space for dialogue
and support, the Center actively contributes to improving the living conditions of Iraqis Montreal.
Thanks to its various programs and its commitment, it is a fundamental pillar for those who seek to
integrate and thrive in their new community. To find out more about the services offered or to
participate in organized activities, do not hesitate to contact the Iraqi Community Center. Together,
let's build a better future for the community Iraqi in Montreal.

Organization 17: Mada Community Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-communautaire-mada/ Website:
https://www.madacentre.com/fr Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 6875
boulevard Décarie, Montréal QC H3W 3E4 514 342-4969 Opening hours SCHEDULE Sunday to
Thursday 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Mission Feed, support and unite the community by providing
meals, furniture and products essential, while creating warm bonds and an atmosphere of hope.
Together we do a difference in the lives of thousands of people every year. Description The Center
Community MADA is an organization dedicated to supporting the community by offering services
essential supplies and assistance to those in need. For over 30 years, MADA has been a source of
generosity and kindness, offering meals, clothing, furniture and much more even more. Services
offered by MADA include: Meals to share: Kosher meals ready to eat employment delivered to
elderly people, people in physical, medical, emotional difficulties or financial, as well as vulnerable
families. Furniture: MADA Furniture Depot offers new and used furniture to help people in need
furnish their homes and create a warm space. Chez Makolet food bank: A market for fresh produce
and food packaged and essential household items offered free of charge to qualified individuals. In
addition of these services, MADA also offers volunteer opportunities for those who wish help reduce
hunger and loneliness in the community. Every year, more than 7,000 people benefit from the help
of MADA, thanks to the commitment of volunteers and donors. The Center Communautaire MADA
is proud to be an organization recommended and rated 5 stars by Charity Intelligence. As a
volunteer or donor, you can help make a difference in the lives of those who need it most. Contact
the MADA Community Center to obtain help, make a donation or become a volunteer. Join our
family and help us create a stronger, more loving and more supportive community. Head office
address: 6875 boulevard Décarie, Montreal, Quebec, H3W 3E4 Telephone: (514) 342-4969 Email:
mada@madacentre.com

Organization 18: Walkley Community Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centrecommunautairewalkley/ Website: None
Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 6650 Ch. Côte Saint-Luc, Montreal QC
H4V 1G8 514-872-1391 Mission The Walkley Center is a non-profit organization managed under
the direction of the provisional Board of Directors including the City of Montreal, Prevention NDG
and NDG Youth Committee. We provide services for the community (children, pre-teens, teens,
adults and seniors). Description The Walkley Community Center, based in Montreal, is a non-profit
organization dedicated to providing essential services to community of all ages. Under the direction
of the Provisional Board of Directors, composed of representatives of the City of Montreal,
Prévention NDG and Comité Jeunesse NDG, our mission is to promote the well-being and
development of our fellow citizens. We intervene mainly in the field of sports and leisure, offering
varied activities for children, pre-teens, teens, adults and seniors. Our community and recreational
center is a place of meeting and exchange where everyone can find activities adapted to their
needs and his desires. Our services include: Sports programs for all ages Leisure activities and
well-being Community and festive events Whether you are looking for a sporting activity, a moment
of relaxation or simply an opportunity to socialize, the Center Walkley Community is the perfect
place for you. Join us and be part of a dynamic and supportive community in Montreal.

Organization 19: CDN – NDG Sports Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-sportif-cdn-ndg/ Website:
https://www.lscdndg.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4880 avenue
Van Horne, Montréal QC H3W 1J3 514 342-9988 Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday
9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., Saturday and Sunday 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Mission Contribute sustainably
to the development of a active and healthy community by inspiring passion for a physically active
lifestyle and healthy, promoting collaboration and inclusion, and offering high quality programs for
the well-being of all. Description CDN-NDG Sports Center is a non-profit organization founded in
1996, located in the Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough in Montreal. Our mission is
to contribute in a sustainable way to the development of an active community and in health. We
